doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Role of bass sax in classic jazz and ballads
summary: He explains Rollini's legacy, playing the Trumbauer-Rollini role with Randy Sandke, and bass sax for ballads and travel difficulties.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Wow. And you’ve been using that on some of the classic jazz, as we see in that recent Jazz Times picture, which is really nice, which we’ll probably insert in this video. Tell me about that particular concert and what is the function of the bass saxophone in that classic jazz?

Well that’s where the instrument has seen its primary use. Of course Adrian Rollini is the acknowledged master of the bass saxophone. He played in the ‘20s on all those great records with Bix Beiderbecke and so that represents sort of the standard by which that type of use of the instrument is measured. And so Randy Sandke does a lot of Bix’s music and Trumbauer and all of that, and he knows I play the C melody too, so I get to sort of be the Trumbauer-Rollini amalgam in those concerts. And it’s a lot of fun. But I like to also use the bass saxophone in other situations where it doesn’t normally get used. It’s a great instrument for ballads. I think it’s the ideal instrument for ballads.
No kidding. Can you see bringing one of those to these kind of festivals some day?

Yeah. I brought one to Decatur, the jazz party there, I brought it. But it is hard to travel with. I could have brought it here if I didn’t need the baritone but they said they wanted a baritone. So I couldn’t really bring both of them. Otherwise if I had a choice I probably would bring a bass sax. It’s great. You know, people are really amazed when you get up with the rhythm section and play a really beautiful “Stardust” or something like that on it © Hamilton Fillius Archive -6-
— everybody says wow — because they’ve never heard that instrument used that way. It’s a great melodic instrument. And it’s great for bebop stuff too, playing fast.
